Frequently Asked Questions

With new subdivisions coming to Woodruff, will service availability change?

Coverage here is an established route, not a new one, and the dispatch already balances town and rural addresses across southern Spartanburg County. Growth adds calls; it does not change response standards. Priority scheduling through the maintenance plan works the same at every address.

Our century home in Woodruff still heats unevenly after a new furnace. Why?

Because the furnace was only part of the system. Uneven heat in older homes usually traces to duct runs, insulation gaps, or room-by-room load differences the equipment cannot correct alone. A whole-system evaluation identifies which is at work, and the fix targets that rather than the equipment again.

Do I need a plumber or an electrician for a standby generator?

Both, and here they arrive as one company. The gas supply line is licensed plumbing work, the transfer switch and connection are licensed electrical work, and sizing happens before either begins. Single-company coordination is the practical advantage: one schedule, one accountable name.

How often should drains be professionally cleaned if nothing is wrong?

There is no calendar requirement for healthy lines; the trigger is behavior, not time. Slowing fixtures, gurgling, or odors mean buildup is narrowing the pipe, and cleaning at that stage prevents the full blockage. Older lines with a history earn a camera check when symptoms start repeating.
